sections.h2: Where is the Person County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Person County Register of Deeds is at 21 Abbitt Street in Roxboro, NC 27573, and the county directory lists (336) 597-1733 as the phone number. It is a separate office from the Tax Office, which sits on the same street at number 13.

The county describes the office as the keeper of the records of Person County and its residents. Its listed services are land record searches, births, deaths and marriages, marriage licenses, notary oaths, and retention of military discharges, cemetery records, grave removals, plats and genealogy material.

  • You search land records here to confirm who holds title before a sale.
  • You record the deed that moves title to a buyer.
  • You record the deed of trust that secures a buyer's loan, and later the satisfaction of your own.

Ask the office for current counter hours and any rules on drop-off or electronic recording before you travel.

sections.h2: Who is the register of deeds, and what does the office do by law?
sections.html:
The register of deeds is an elected county officer, chosen by the county's voters every two years (G.S. 161-1). The office records instruments of conveyance, collects the uniform fees, and collects the deed excise tax before a deed is recorded (G.S. 161-10).

The office does not draft deeds or give legal advice, and it does not decide who owns what. It indexes what is presented to it in the order received. That order carries legal weight. A conveyance, contract to convey, option, lease longer than three years, or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the time of registration (G.S. 47-18).

For a Person County seller, the lesson is simple. A deed that is signed but unrecorded protects no one against a later recorded document. Have the closing attorney confirm recording the same day as funding.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Person County?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets recording fees for every county, and the register of deeds cannot charge more or less. A general instrument such as a deed costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for up to 35 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page.

Uniform recording fees collected by the Person County Register of Deeds under G.S. 161-10
ItemFee printed in the statute
General instrument, first 15 pages$26.00
Each extra page of a general instrument$4.00
Deed of trust or mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat, per sheet$21.00
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00
Extra instrument in one document$10.00 each

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed.

sections.h2: How does the transfer tax work when a Person County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The excise tax on a deed is $1.00 for each $500.00 of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed, with any fraction of $500.00 counted as a full unit (G.S. 105-228.30). The statute puts the duty on the transferor, the person giving up title, who pays the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded.

If a parcel lies in more than one county, the tax goes to the county that holds the greater value. Half of what the office collects stays in the county general fund, and the other half, less refunds and an allowance, goes to the Department of Revenue each month.

  • The seller normally pays, so it lowers the seller's net proceeds.
  • The tax is figured on the price or value stated in the transaction, so confirm the number with your closing attorney.
  • Ask the register of deeds how the office treats a deed with little or no stated consideration, such as a transfer between family members.

sections.h2: What should a Person County seller check before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Check the chain of title, the legal description, and any open liens. Search the Person County land records for deeds of trust that were never marked satisfied, for judgments, and for any contract or option recorded against the land.

If the sale involves a contract for deed under Chapter 47H, the seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days of signing (Chapter 47H). Skipping that step leaves the buyer's interest exposed to later purchasers.

  • Match the names on the deed to the names on the last recorded deed.
  • Confirm that each loan is released of record before closing, since satisfactions carry no recording fee.
  • Bring the unpaid property tax figure from the Tax Office to the closing so the lien is cleared.

A cash buyer can often close without waiting on a lender, which helps when title questions are small and fixable. A cloud on title, such as an unrecorded estate, takes a court or attorney to fix first.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for Person County property?
faqs.a: Record it with the Person County Register of Deeds at 21 Abbitt Street in Roxboro, NC 27573. The county directory lists (336) 597-1733 for the office.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a deed in Person County?
faqs.a: State law sets it at $26.00 for up to 15 pages and $4.00 for each additional page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 for up to 35 pages plus $4.00 per extra page.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Person County deed?
faqs.a: The transferor, usually the seller, pays it to the register of deeds before recording. The rate is $1.00 per $500.00 of consideration or value, with any fraction of $500.00 counted in full.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No, the state fee schedule lists no charge for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages.

faqs.q: Does recording order matter in North Carolina?
faqs.a: Yes, an unrecorded conveyance does not protect against lien creditors or buyers for value, and priority runs by the time of registration in the county where the land lies.
